title: Python & NumPy for ML
why: Every ML library is arrays underneath. Fast, correct array code is the foundation for everything else.
explain: A NumPy array is a block of typed memory with a shape. Operations on whole arrays (vectorization) run in compiled loops, so replacing a Python for-loop over samples with array math is typically 10-100x faster.

Broadcasting lets arrays of different shapes combine: shapes are compared from the right, and each dimension must match or be 1. Subtracting a (n_features,) mean vector from a (n_samples, n_features) matrix just works. Most shape bugs come from forgetting which axis you are reducing over: axis=0 collapses rows (one result per column), axis=1 collapses columns (one result per row).
Learn to think in shapes. Write the shape of every array in a comment. A matrix multiply (n, d) @ (d, k) gives (n, k), and that single operation is the core of linear models and neural networks.
key_points: Vectorize: avoid Python loops over samples
Broadcasting aligns shapes from the right; dimensions must match or be 1
axis=0 reduces down the rows, axis=1 across the columns; keepdims=True preserves rank
Slicing returns views; fancy indexing returns copies
pitfalls: A (n,) array combined with an (n, 1) array silently broadcasts to (n, n)
Integer dtype arrays truncate float results unless you cast

leetcode.why: Reshaping is the everyday NumPy operation; do it by index math to understand what reshape really does.
Transpose swaps axes; the same idea is behind X.T in every gradient formula.
In-place matrix index manipulation builds comfort with 2D array coordinates.
Prefix and suffix products are the loop-free pattern behind cumulative operations (cumprod/cumsum).
2D prefix sums (integral images) give O(1) region sums and reappear in computer vision.

industry.q: Without loops, how would you compute the pairwise Euclidean distance matrix between two sets of points? Explain the shapes involved.
key_points: Expand (a-b)^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab, or broadcast with new axes
Broadcasting to (n,m,d) costs memory; the dot-product form does not
Clip tiny negative values from float error before the square root

industry.q: Implement softmax for a (batch, classes) matrix so that it does not overflow on large logits.
key_points: Subtract the row max before exponentiating
Use keepdims=True so the division broadcasts
Mention log-sum-exp when you need log-probabilities

industry.q: A teammate's feature-normalization code gives wrong results only when the dataset has a single column. What shape bug do you suspect?
key_points: A 1-D array vs a 2-D (n,1) array handled differently
reshape(-1, 1) or keepdims to stabilize shapes
Add shape assertions and a one-column unit test
